solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Olympic sport community gutted? Hang on

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides taken out, so only the shell of the word survives

blocks.note: a city is a community; only its first and last letters remain
to cling is to hang on tight

explanation.surface: An Olympic competitor's home town has been emptied out, and someone is told to hold tight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'gutted' makes it read like a comment on the community; it is the instruction to keep only the end letters of a word for community.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and road racing on bicycles are Olympic events, so the pastime counts as an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Novice is heading for mastery in artistic style

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a cub is a beginner, as in cub reporter
taken as written
the first letter of mastery

explanation.surface: A beginner is on the way to mastering a particular way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism is the early twentieth-century art movement of Picasso and Braque, a style of painting.

clue.text: Touch of cayenne? It's foul mixed with a fruit dessert

indicators.note: a touch of something is just a small amount, here its first letter
mixed means stirred together into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of cayenne
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook complains that a pinch of hot pepper ruins a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed with' reads like a recipe instruction; 'mixed' acts on IT'S FOUL plus A, and 'with' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clafoutis is a French baked pudding of cherries or other fruit set in batter.

clue.text: Deeply emotional writer worried opening of novel is boring

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
boring here means drilling into, so a letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: the setter writing the clue refers to themself as I
the first letter of novel
tense means anxious, worried

explanation.surface: An anxious author fears the start of their novel is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like a verdict on the novel's opening; it means drilling, so N bores into I TENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and deep, so an intense person is deeply emotional.

clue.text: Spoilt girl shortened sarong made of silk material

indicators.note: a shortened word has lost its tail letter
something spoilt has been ruined and thrown out of its proper order

blocks.note: girl without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoilt girl takes up the hem of her sarong, made of silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt girl' reads as a brat; 'Spoilt' is the anagram signal for GIR plus SARONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Grosgrain is a heavy ribbed fabric, traditionally of silk, used for ribbons and trimmings.

clue.text: Priest with European in Irish parliament turning to see what's said?

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the parliament's name is read from right to left
in places the priest and the European inside the parliament's name

blocks.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
PR is a standard abbreviation for priest
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A priest and a European colleague in the Dáil seem to be changing direction on some issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil (Dáil Éireann) is the Irish lower house; reversed it gives LIAD, which wraps PR + E to make LIPREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading lets a deaf person understand speech by watching mouth movements, so they see words spoken; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Twirling this will contribute to gaucho's salary?

definitions.text: Twirling this will contribute to gaucho's salary?

indicators.note: the answer contributes some of the letters of the following words, so it lies within them
twirling spins it round, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A cowboy's rope-twirling skill earns him his pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaucho is a South American cowboy; the whole clue describes the rope he twirls, while the letters hide backwards across 'gaucho's salary'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is the looped rope a cowboy spins and throws to catch cattle, the tool of his trade.

clue.text: Flashy newcomer quietly runs into street releasing energy

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so a letter is set free from the word
into places the letter inside the street word

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical term for quietly
an avenue is a street
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An ostentatious new arrival slips quietly onto the road, all energy spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releasing energy' removes just one E from the street, not every E; 'p' for quietly is the musical piano marking.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a social upstart who has newly gained wealth and tends to show it off.

clue.text: Terms for the sensation when you and I get bored

definitions.text: Terms for the sensation when you and I get bored

blocks.clueFragment: Terms for the sensation when you and I get bored
blocks.note: surface reading: words describing a feeling the two of us share when bored
setter's reading: the word for boredom has its terms, its final letters, sounding like you and I

explanation.surface: Someone asks what word names the feeling we both get when we are bored.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a French loan for boredom, and its last two letters are U and I, the 'you and I' of the clue; 'Terms' points at those ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and dissatisfaction, the feeling of being bored.

clue.text: Performer attached to drink in decline

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a turn is a variety act or performer

explanation.surface: An entertainer who has taken to the bottle is on the slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attached to' puts the performer after the drink. A turn is an old music-hall word for an act on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in activity or fortunes, especially an economic decline.

clue.text: Attractive lover, in our opinion, should retain trace of enchantment

indicators.note: a mere trace of a word is just its first letter
to retain is to hold inside, so the opinion phrase keeps a letter within it

blocks.note: a beau is a boyfriend or lover
'to us' means in our view
the first letter of enchantment

explanation.surface: We think our handsome partner ought to keep a little of the magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In our opinion' is not padding: it gives two short words, read together as one chunk that holds the trace.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauteous is a poetic word for beautiful, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Father leaves Scottish town to start again

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place they are no longer in it, so these letters drop out

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
Renfrew is a town near Glasgow

explanation.surface: A priest moves away from a town in Scotland to make a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: Take FR out of RENFREW, a town just west of Glasgow, and RENEW is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to begin it afresh, resume it after a break.

clue.text: Refuse to accept introduction of speaker's banal material

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of speaker
corn is trite, hackneyed stuff, as in corny

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a speech because its opening material is tired and clichéd.
explanation.walkthrough: Corn in the sense of sentimental or trite material is what makes something corny.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn an offer is to reject it with contempt, refusing to accept it.

clue.text: Surveyor to leave and stop collecting earth

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the word for leave holds a letter

blocks.note: to go is to leave
E is the abbreviation for earth
to desist is to stop

explanation.surface: A surveyor is told to pack up and quit, taking soil samples with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' looks like soil in the surface, but it is the single-letter abbreviation used in physics and on plugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesist measures the shape and size of the Earth, a specialist kind of surveyor.

clue.text: Helps set up art works — famous example here

definitions.note: 'here' points back to the art works just named

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and shape it, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone helping hang an exhibition notes that a celebrated painting is among the pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art works' reads as a noun phrase, but 'works' is the anagram signal acting on the four words before it, and the result is itself a famous art work.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's mural of Christ's final meal is one of the best-known paintings in the world.

clue.text: Play electronic dance music, swamping noise from bullring?

indicators.note: to swamp is to engulf, surrounding something completely

blocks.note: trance is a genre of electronic dance music
olé is the shout of the crowd at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A DJ plays electronic dance music loudly enough to drown out the crowd at a bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like the verb for the DJ; it is the definition, the noun meaning slack in a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, play and tolerance both mean the permitted looseness or allowance between moving parts.

clue.text: Left Tesla, stealing inventions supporting largest corporation

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so the outer letters hold the middle ones

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
lies are made-up stories
T is the symbol for the tesla, a unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Reads like business news: a departed Tesla figure took inventions to back a huge company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so the definition means carrying the biggest paunch. PORT and T hold LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout, so the portliest person bears the biggest belly, playfully called a corporation.

clue.text: Prosecutors upset about radio broadcast appearing intermittently

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read bottom to top
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
about means surrounding, so the prosecutors go round the other letters

blocks.note: the CPS is the Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawyers are annoyed about a radio programme that keeps cutting in and out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crown Prosecution Service brings criminal prosecutions in England and Wales. In a down clue 'upset' turns its initials upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals, now and then rather than continuously.

clue.text: Die clutching one fine, less important religious symbol

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tight inside one's grip

blocks.note: to pass on is a euphemism for die
the Roman numeral for one
F is short for fine, as on pencil leads
lower means of lesser rank

explanation.surface: A dying person grips a fine and something of lesser importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' is a two-word phrase here, a euphemism, split to hold the numeral. Missionaries read the flower's parts as the instruments of Christ's Passion.
explanation.definitionFit: The passiflora bloom was named for its symbolism of the crucifixion: crown of thorns, nails and wounds.

clue.text: I blush to admit name being overlooked

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so a letter goes inside the blush phrase

blocks.note: taken as written
to blush is to go red
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone confesses with embarrassment that their name was left off the list.
explanation.walkthrough: GO RED takes N after its first letter: G(N)ORED, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignored means disregarded or passed over, exactly the sense of being overlooked.

clue.text: Swimwear: you worry about it

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the words for you and worry read backwards

blocks.note: U is text-speak for you
to stew is to fret or worry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A swimmer is told they are fretting over their costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry about it' looks like one phrase, but 'about' turns back only the first two words, and 'it' is added unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A wetsuit is the close-fitting rubber garment worn by divers, surfers and open-water swimmers.

clue.text: Continue to be pierced by rejection — that is a sense of hopelessness

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven through its middle

blocks.note: am, as in 'I am', means continue to exist
no is the word of refusal
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Persistent rejection leaves someone feeling there is no hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continue to be' means to exist, as in Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomie is a sociological term for alienation and despair when social norms break down.

clue.text: Company enthralled by diatribe regret lying about story-teller

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive within its spell
lying about suggests turned round, so the word for regret is read backwards

blocks.note: a rant is an angry tirade
Co is the abbreviation for company
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A firm is gripped by an angry outburst about regrets, with some falsehoods mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests falsehood, but 'lying about' means laid the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone skilled at telling anecdotes, a teller of stories.

clue.text: Was offered old part requiring little acting

blocks.note: a chance that came your way was offered to you
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An actor was offered a role that needs hardly any performing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor in a film or play, a small role.

clue.text: South African creature? Stop circling borders of Liberia

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters
circling means going round, so the stop word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: to end is to stop
the first and last letters of Liberia

explanation.surface: An African animal is halted on its way round the edges of Liberia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the eland lives across much of Africa, not just the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large spiral-horned antelope found on the plains of southern and eastern Africa.

clue.text: Claw back a bit of tax before extended cut

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the two letters read right to left
a bit of a word is just its first letter
something cut has had its end lopped off

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of tax
long means drawn out, extended

explanation.surface: Reads like a demand to claw back some tax ahead of a longer-term reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Claw back' looks like a phrase meaning recover; the definition is just 'Claw', and 'back' reverses A and T. LONG then loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Knocked back wine stifling expression of hesitation or objection

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, holding something inside
knocked back suggests pushed backwards, so the result reads in reverse

blocks.note: red is a wine
um is the noise people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone downing wine swallows their doubts and misgivings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back wine' reads as a drinker's action; 'knocked back' is the reversal of R(UM)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A demur is a protest or show of reluctance, so it means an objection.

clue.text: Notice fellow returning outside exercise area over and over again

indicators.note: returning means heading back, so the word for fellow is read backwards
outside means wrapped around, so the fellow goes round the other words

blocks.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a man is a fellow
to exercise a right is to use it
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone spots a man coming back past the gym yard again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise area' reads as one place, like a yard, but splits into USE and A, which sit inside NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for 'to the point of sickness', used of something repeated tediously.

clue.text: Obscure recording includes deafening conclusion of piece

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
deafening noise is extremely loud
the last letter of piece

explanation.surface: An unknown recording features a very noisy ending to the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the recording; it is the definition, read as a past-participle sense of hidden or dimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouded means made dim or unclear, as an issue is obscured or befogged.

clue.text: Space on printed page journalist finally filled covering style

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
something filled has had material put inside it

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space half an em wide
tiles cover roofs and floors
the last letter of journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist finally fills a blank space on a printed page with something about fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's unit of space half an em wide. 'Style' is the verb meaning to give a title to.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or title, which is what entitle means in that sense.
